correctness.rationale: The exact polar cube-section vertex classification proves all cycle facets are simplices for odd n and balanced two-simplex free sums for even n, with dimensions and independence checked. A stand-alone all-parameter gauge calculation proves λ(Q_{p,q})=1/(p+q−2), with explicit boundary points excluding larger weights. Known face inheritance and centrally symmetric boundary lifting (Artstein-Avidan et al., Lemmas 2.2 and 5.1) then yield both optimal inequalities for all n≥3. CHECK.py verifies 1,154 signed facet patterns across n=3..10 and 4,120 exact rational free-sum samples with exact strict obstruction witnesses, but these tests do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 definition and general face/boundary inheritance theorems are credited, as are 2018/2021 cycle-edge facet theory. The checked source materials do not give an exact Schneider index of a cycle symmetric-edge polytope, nor the required free-sum covering lemma. The new exact two-block gauge calculation yields the parity formula. Three same-invariant published full RESULT.md records were examined: their cross-polytope skeleton, hypersimplex, and parity-cube problems are not the signed cycle-root polytope and their bounds do not imply its index. Historical priority is provisional; no global uniqueness is claimed.

value.rationale: The Schneider vertex-generation index quantifies the smallest homothetic vertex-copy cover of an entire natural convex body. Computing it for all cycle symmetric-edge polytopes exposes a genuine parity-dependent shift tied to simplicial versus two-simplex free-sum facets. The same proof establishes a sharp reusable convexification lemma for arbitrary free sums of two centered simplices. This is an exact structural classification and not merely a one-instance table, a general textbook projection or a known parameter renamed.
